title: Tensor–Hom form of the exchange
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type
$k$-schemes, with $f^!=Rf^!$ the constructible exceptional adjoint of
[sk-def-sf-operations] (vi) (no admissibility datum is assumed), and let
$M\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ and $N\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
Rf_*\RHom_X(M,f^!N)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\RHom_Y(Rf_!M,N),
$$

in the ambient category $D^+(Y,\Lambda)$, natural in $M$ and $N$ and
compatible with finite reduction, scalar extension and shifts.

proof.text:
First establish the actual tensor–Hom bijection, rather than take it from a definition of the operations. On any of the small ringed sites $\mathcal C$ in the datum, write $H(P,Q)=R\mathcal Hom(P,Q)$. The two cited statements give, naturally in $L,P,Q$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(L,H(P,Q))
\cong H^0(\mathcal C,H(L,H(P,Q)))
\cong H^0(\mathcal C,H(L\otimes^L P,Q))
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L\otimes^L P,Q).$$
The outer bijections are the global-sections identification and the middle one is internal-Hom currying. Interchanging the tensor factors gives the convention $P\otimes^L L$ used below. These bijections are the adjunction with evaluation as counit. At finite coefficients this is the ambient, uncompleted tensor–Hom adjunction; no site-perfectness assumption is made.

source.place: The displayed chain and Yoneda conclusion, refined using the named ringed-site, constructible-preservation and coefficient statements.

proof.text:
At $R=\mathcal O_E$, let $P,L,Q$ be integral bounded constructible objects on a scheme $W$, and put $T=P\otimes^L_{\widehat R_W}L$, using the ordinary ambient tensor only in this paragraph. The completed tensor in the datum is
$$P\widehat\otimes^L_R L=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(P_n\otimes^L_{A_n}L_n).$$
Its tower is the quotient tower of $T$: on K-flat representatives, the balancing isomorphism is $(p\otimes a)\otimes(l\otimes b)\mapsto(p\otimes l)\otimes ab$, with inverse $(p\otimes l)\otimes a\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes(l\otimes a)$. It commutes with differentials and quotient transitions. The constant/completed-coefficient comparison identifies this quotient limit, with its unit, with the Koszul completion of $T$ over $\widehat R_W$. It also identifies the local and Koszul completeness conditions. The integral definition makes $Q$ isomorphic to a quotient limit of its reductions; that limit is a completion by the same comparison, hence $Q$ satisfies the local completeness condition needed by the reflector. Apply the reflector's mapping property, then step 1:
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P\widehat\otimes^L_R L,Q)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes^L_{\widehat R_W}L,Q)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L,H(P,Q)).$$
Every arrow is natural and induced by the completion unit or evaluation. This proves the needed completed tensor–Hom adjunction by composing existing statements; it does not identify the two tensor objects. The Noetherian coefficient ring is $R$, the ideal is $(\varpi_E)$, and the site is small, exactly as required by the cited completion comparison and reflector. The coefficient DVR lemma makes $R$ a principal ideal domain, hence Noetherian because each ideal has one generator.

proof.text: At $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ put $A_{M,N}=Rf_*H(M,f^!N)$ and $B_{M,N}=H(Rf_!M,N)$. The unconditional constructible exceptional adjunction puts $f^!N$ and $Rf_!M$ in $D^b_{ctf}$. Choose nonnegative dimension bounds $d_X,d_Y$ using the finite-type dimension lemma (zero for an empty scheme). For $W=X,Y$, finite type gives a finite affine cover $W=\bigcup_iU_i$ with $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_i$ for finitely generated $k$-algebras $C_i$. Each chart is Noetherian by the affine Noetherian lemma. A descending chain of closed subsets of $W$ stabilizes on each chart, hence globally after the maximum of the finitely many stabilization indices. Thus $W$ meets the Noetherian hypothesis of the finite-cover locality lemma. An affine chart is separated over $k$, since its diagonal is defined by the surjection $C_i\otimes_kC_i\to C_i$, and its dimension is at most $d_W$ by open-subspace monotonicity.

proof.text: Apply the finite internal-Hom corollary on each separated affine chart to the pairs $(M,f^!N)$ and $(Rf_!M,N)$ on their respective schemes. Their input Tor intervals restrict unchanged: for a degree-zero module sheaf $F$ on $U_i$, extension by zero is degree zero and restricts back to $F$; exact restriction and the derived tensor-pullback comparison give $(K\otimes^Lj_{i,!}F)|_{U_i}\cong K|_{U_i}\otimes^LF$. The same exact restriction preserves cohomology, and each finite constructible stratification restricts to its intersections with $U_i$. Thus the local inputs satisfy all hypotheses of the corollary. For input intervals $[a,b]$ and $[c,e]$ it gives bounded constructible internal Homs with the common interval $[c-b-2d_W,e-a+2d_W]$. The ringed-site internal-Hom restriction isomorphism identifies these outputs with the restrictions of the actual global internal Homs.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-finite-cover-ctf-locality] to each global internal Hom, with the Noetherian cover from step 3 and the common interval from step 4. Its statement gives bounded constructibility and that Tor interval globally, exactly the conditions of the finite constructibility and finite-Tor definitions. Apply [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale] to $H(M,f^!N)$, using the given separated finite-type $f$ and dimension bound $d_X$. Consequently both $A_{M,N}$ and $B_{M,N}$ lie in the full category $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$. For an empty cover the locality lemma gives the zero object. No separatedness of $X$ or $Y$ over $k$, properness of $f$, or site-perfectness of the inputs is used.

proof.text: For $\Lambda=R=\mathcal O_E$, the unconditional constructible adjunction puts $f^!N$ and $Rf_!M$ in $D^b_{ctf}$. For each of the two pairs $(M,f^!N)$ on $X$ and $(Rf_!M,N)$ on $Y$, restrict to a finite affine cover of the relevant scheme $W$. On an affine chart use the integral internal-Hom corollary and the finite-level uniform bounds of steps 3–5; restriction of internal Hom is its ringed-site restriction comparison. Choose one dimension bound $d_W$ for all charts. The common finite-reduction Tor interval from that corollary bounds the nonzero cohomology on every chart. Global constructibility is obtained by the finite disjoint refinement $U_i\setminus\bigcup_{j<i}U_j$ as in steps 3–5. Internal Hom into a derived-complete object is derived complete, and its integral reduction is the evaluation-defined comparison of the integral Hom-reduction lemma. Thus both internal Homs meet the integral definition globally, also when $W$ is not separated. Apply integral direct-image constructibility to $H=H(M,f^!N)$; its statement gives completeness, finite-reduction comparisons and a bound independent of $n$. Finally the residue-Tor theorem identifies $D^b_c(Y,R)$ with $D^b_{ctf}(Y,R)$. Consequently both $A_{M,N}$ and $B_{M,N}$ belong to the same full category used for Yoneda. This argument keeps completed coefficient sheaves distinct from constant integral or condensed coefficients.

source.place: The displayed chain and Yoneda conclusion, refined using the named ringed-site, constructible-preservation and coefficient statements.

proof.text:
Let $\Lambda$ now be finite or integral and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. Using the adjunctions from steps 1–2, the projection isomorphism, and the ordinary adjunction and the unconditional constructible exceptional adjunction, form the natural bijection $h_L$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_Y(L,B_{M,N})
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!M\otimes^L L,N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!(M\otimes^L Lf^*L),N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(M\otimes^L Lf^*L,f^!N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(Lf^*L,H(M,f^!N))\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(L,A_{M,N}).
\end{aligned}$$
At the integral stage every tensor in this chain is completed tensor. For the second arrow precompose with $\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,L}^{-1}$: its direction is from $Rf_!(M\otimes^LLf^*L)$ to $Rf_!M\otimes^LL$. The projection theorem needs $M$ bounded constructible and $L$ finite-Tor, both available. All intermediate inputs to the exceptional adjunction are finite-Tor and bounded constructible: the finite-Tor pullback lemma applies to $L$ and gives bounded constructibility of $Lf^*L$, tensor with the finite-Tor $M$ preserves it, and integral pullback and completed tensor preserve it by their integral preservation theorem. At integral coefficients the residue-Tor theorem upgrades the constructible outputs to the uniform finite-Tor domain. Hence the constructible exceptional adjunction applies here. For the exceptional arrow use the new constructible-adjunction lemma, which has exactly these coefficient categories and requires no ambient-adjoint datum. The last arrow is the ordinary pullback–direct-image adjunction on bounded constructible objects. These checks justify every bijection without invoking the preservation summary that depends back on this item.

proof.text: The projection isomorphism used above is the actual coefficient-stage projection map: at $A_{E,n}$ it is the finite etale theorem, transported to pro-etale realizations by the pro-etale projection theorem; at $R$ it is the compatible normalized-system isomorphism of the adic theorem; at $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ it is the rational/common-stage projection theorem. The all-stage projection-formula interface identifies these maps and records their coefficient compatibilities. Thus the second bijection uses the inverse of the map with direction $Rf_!M\otimes^LL\to Rf_!(M\otimes^LLf^*L)$, with both $M,L$ finite-Tor; it never applies a projection theorem to an arbitrary bounded-below test object.

proof.text:
Apply the fully faithful Yoneda embedding to the full category $\mathcal C=D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, which contains both objects by steps 3–6. The natural bijections $h_L$ identify $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(-,B_{M,N})$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(-,A_{M,N})$. Explicitly set
$$a=h_{B_{M,N}}(1_{B_{M,N}}):B_{M,N}\to A_{M,N},\qquad
b=h_{A_{M,N}}^{-1}(1_{A_{M,N}}):A_{M,N}\to B_{M,N}.$$
Naturality in $L$ says $h_L(u)=a\circ u$ and $h_L^{-1}(v)=b\circ v$. Thus $ab=1_A$ and $ba=1_B$. The required canonical isomorphism has forward map $b$. Naturality of the five bijections in $M$ (contravariantly) and $N$ (covariantly) implies naturality of this isomorphism by the uniqueness part of Yoneda. In particular no extension-by-zero generator theorem, geometric-stalk detection, or unproved equivalence of whole sites is needed.

proof.text: For finite quotients, the internal-Hom comparison is evaluation-defined. Restrict it to the finite affine covers of step 3 and apply [thm-coef-finite-hom] to the restricted finite-Tor inputs. Internal-Hom restriction commutes with this construction. Exact restriction commutes with cohomology; if the cone restricts to zero on every member of the cover, each of its cohomology sheaves is zero by the sheaf axiom. This proves invertibility of the global comparison. For the ordinary direct-image comparison use [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]. Its pro-etale clause applies: [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] gives an etale bounded constructible witness for $H(M,f^!N)$, and [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii) gives that witness the same finite Tor interval. Integral reduction of internal Hom is the evaluation-defined comparison of [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction]; integral direct-image reduction is [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible]. These are actual invertible comparisons on our domains. This locality argument checks invertibility, not equality of derived morphisms.

proof.text: For finite scalar extension $E\subset E'$, put $A=A_n$ and $B=\mathcal O_{E'}/\varpi^n\mathcal O_{E'}$. The coefficient-system adjoint lemma says $B$ is finite free over $A$. Apply [lem-sf-ringed-finite-free-hom-base-change] on each small ringed site to the constant ring sheaves $A\to B$: its hypotheses require only finite freeness and its conclusion is precisely the evaluation-defined internal-Hom comparison, natural in both variables. Thus it intertwines tensor-Hom transposes, with no site-perfectness hypothesis. The finite direct-image coefficient lemma applies to this finite $A$-algebra $B$ and gives the counit-defined comparison. If $e=e(E'/E)$, then $B=A_{E',en}$ by the exceptional-adjunction coefficient statement. A further quotient is therefore the finite-quotient case of step 10 over $E'$. The coefficient cocycles in that statement identify the composite exceptional comparisons.

proof.text: For integral scalar extension $E\subset E'$, [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] supplies the internal-Hom and tensor comparisons on the bounded constructible integral inputs. For ordinary direct image, [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies scalar extension with ordinary tensor by the completed coefficient sheaf, finite free of rank $[E':E]$. Choose a basis. Under restriction of scalars this tensor is a finite direct sum. The ordinary direct-image functor is additive, hence carries a finite biproduct to the corresponding biproduct; the same holds for its derived functor, since a finite sum of K-injective resolutions is K-injective (the Hom complex from an acyclic complex is the finite sum of acyclic Hom complexes). The strict-tower derived limit also preserves finite biproducts, as an exact additive functor. Hence the canonical integral scalar/direct-image map is invertible. The basis tests invertibility only: the specified map is adjoint to extension of the old counit, so its normalization is basis independent. The finite-free internal-Hom lemma applied to the completed ring sheaves identifies the scalar Hom map with the evaluation transpose; the completed-scalar comparison identifies this with integral scalar extension.

proof.text: Check coefficient compatibility for the specified forward map $b:A\to B$ by transposition. Its action on a test map $u:L\to A$ is: transpose by $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$; transpose tensor--Hom to a map $M\otimes^LLf^*L\to f^!N$; transpose by the constructible exceptional adjunction; precompose with $\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,L}$; transpose tensor--Hom again. For a coefficient functor $T$, insert the canonical comparisons at these five places. The operation-reduction statement identifies tensor, ordinary unit/counit and compact-support comparisons. The unconditional constructible-adjunction lemma gives the explicit unit/counit equations for the exceptional comparison. The projection-formula theorem gives its coefficient square. Internal-Hom comparisons are the transposes of coefficient change of evaluation; they therefore identify the two tensor--Hom transpositions, by their defining universal property. Thus the two composites from $T(A)$ to the new $B$ have the same tensor/evaluation/counit transpose and are equal. This is a global transposition calculation, not an inference that equality of derived maps can be checked on an open cover. The operation-reduction statement and the exceptional-adjunction statement supply their comparisons on these domains; steps 10–12 established invertibility of the Hom and ordinary direct-image comparisons in question. The two tensor-Hom comparisons are evaluation transposes, so the two coefficient-change paths have identical transposes at each of the five arrows. Injectivity of the adjunction bijections identifies their composite maps. This proves the finite-reduction and scalar-extension squares for $b$. Field reduction always refers to an integral representative before localization.

proof.text:
The shift compatibility is checked on the same Hom bijection. Under the canonical shift identifications, for any integer $r$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(L,A_{M,N[r]})\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L[-r],A_{M,N}),\qquad
\operatorname{Hom}(L,B_{M,N[r]})\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L[-r],B_{M,N}).$$
The five arrows for $(L,N[r])$ identify with those for $(L[-r],N)$: a tensor factor shifted by $r$ shifts the tensor by $r$, and each exact right adjoint's shift comparison is the transpose of the corresponding comparison for its left adjoint. The tensor–Hom comparisons have the signs of the shifted Hom complex; shifting its first variable gives $H(M[r],Q)=H(M,Q)[-r]$, while shifting its second gives $H(M,Q[r])=H(M,Q)[r]$. Both transposition routes therefore use the same signed evaluation map. In the projection definition, the proper projection map is the transpose of $(\varepsilon_p\otimes1)\circ\mu_p$, and the compact-support map is its composite with $Rp_*(\gamma)$, where $\gamma$ is the extension-by-zero tensor comparison followed by pullback composition. Shifting either tensor factor shifts each of these composites by the total-tensor convention, using $d_{C[r]}=(-1)^rd_C$; the evaluation comparison uses that same convention. The shifted composite is therefore the specified shifted projection transformation. Thus $h$ for the shifted arguments is the shifted $h$. By uniqueness in step 9 this proves the shift square for the exchange, in the second variable and, with the negative shift, in the first. Completion commutes with these identifications since its Koszul-limit construction is exact and the completion unit is natural.

proof.text: Pass to the two field stages using their actual definitions. Rationalization keeps the integral objects and replaces each Hom group by its tensor product with $E$. Send the inverse pair $(a,b)$ of step 9 to its images there; their composites remain identities. The integral tensor–Hom bijection and its naturality localize, and the prescribed operations on objects and morphisms are the ones of the datum, so this gives the displayed exchange over $E$. For $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, represent the finitely many input objects and maps over a common finite extension $E$. Define the exchange by its $E$-stage map. Steps 10–13 identifies this representative after any larger finite extension, so its class is independent of the representative. The inverse is represented by the inverse at that same stage; naturality and the coefficient and shift equations hold over a common stage and therefore in the directed colimit of Hom groups. This supplies every coefficient stage in the statement without using a theorem on integral or field exceptional adjoints that depends back on this item.

split_report.summary: Repair of the dedicated N1 handoff for long steps 3 and 8. Retained the statement, Lean record, proof route and all other arguments, updating numerical references. Replaced finite-cover gluing by the existing lem-sf-finite-cover-ctf-locality and finite-free derived Hom scalar change by the existing lem-sf-ringed-finite-free-hom-base-change. Expanded the two old steps into short applications and coefficient checks; no new nodes. Exact restriction is now cited explicitly. Every non-elementary step is at most 2000 characters.

Repairs isolate the hidden arguments of former steps 3 and 8 by citing their now-existing supporting nodes.
